subject: Sampling exemption request for short-term retention pilot / audit evidence routing
messages:
From: DataHealth Security <security@datahealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence sampling exemption for pilot

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are greenlighting a 6-week pilot but need a quick exception for audit evidence sampling: our auditors require that all transactions touching PHI be retained for 90 days in raw form for a short window. Your standard audit-stream sampling at 10% will not meet our audit scope for the pilot.

Can Redwood temporarily mark the pilot workspace as "full-evidence mode" (no sampling) for events related to the ingestion and inference paths for the next 8 weeks? We understand the cost implications and are prepared to accept a one-time usage surcharge.

Specific asks:
- A way to opt a workspace into full audit-stream retention for a date range
- A simple proof-of-delivery (evidence pack) around the end of the pilot with event slices by time
- Confirmation that BYOK-held keys remain enforced for any persisted artifacts

Attaching a short pilot scope spreadsheet. Let us know what information you need from our side.

Best,
Samir Patel
Head of Security, DataHealth
(attachment: pilot_scope.xlsx)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: security@datahealth.com
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence sampling exemption for pilot

Marissa / Karthik — looped in since this looks like a cross-product ask (audit stream + retention + BYOK).

TL;DR: DataHealth wants a short-term opt-in to disable sampling for a specific workspace/date range and a delivered evidence pack at pilot end. They are OK with a surcharge.

Questions I have for the triage:
- Ops: can we support a per-workspace toggle to turn off sampling for a bounded date range without an infra deploy? If not, what is the minimal engineering scope?
- Security: BYOK enforcement on persisted evidence — confirm there are no shortcuts that would cause keys to be escrowed or copied to Redwood-managed KMS during the evidence export process.
- Product: what UI/API surface and audit log flags do we need to expose for the customer and for our own auditability?

I attached DataHealth's pilot_scope.xlsx and a draft evidence_sample_config.yaml (very rough).

Can folks reply with rough feasibility + a proposed owner and ETA? I'll coordinate comms to DataHealth and confirm surcharge language with Ben if this is feasible.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Product Manager, Compliance Features
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence sampling exemption for pilot

Short answer: feasible with caveats.

Notes from infra side:
- Sampling is applied at the stream router layer. We do have a per-workspace sampling override flag in our config, but it is not surfaced in the Console API today (it was added for incident-mode ops). We can repurpose that flag for a temporary opt-in.
- Work required: add a guarded API endpoint + an internal approval workflow (safety lock) so ops can flip the flag and revert automatically after X days. Estimate: 3 engineer-weeks to do this safely (api + audit trail + scheduled revert).
- Storage cost: full-event retention will increase S3/Blob usage; need finance listing for surcharge.
- Evidence pack export: we can generate time-bounded event slices and package them as ndjson or parquet. That export path currently writes to an intermediate Redwood-managed bucket; supporting direct-to-customer BYOK output will need one more week to wire up (we must ensure no key material touches Redwood-managed KMS).

Risks / blockers:
- If we export to a Redwood-managed staging bucket for packaging, BYOK guarantees are weakened. I recommend we implement direct-to-customer export to a customer-provided bucket (requires new IAM flow).
- Operational load for rollback if the sampled flag is toggled incorrectly.

Proposal:
1) Short-term (fast): Use the existing internal override flag but require an SRE oncall approval and manual revert at +8 weeks. This is 1 engineer-day to schedule and test. Evidence export will be to a Redwood staging area (fast) — acceptable only if DataHealth signs an attestation acknowledging staging and escrow constraints.
2) Medium-term (safer): Build the API + scheduled revert + direct-to-customer BYOK export (3-4w).

I'll volunteer to own the infra estimate and the implementation plan if we get signoff.

-karthik

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2027 14:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence sampling exemption for pilot

Thanks Karthik — that breakdown helps. A few product/security clarifications from my side: 

1) BYOK: we must make explicit that any exported evidence targeted at a Redwood staging bucket is encrypted at-rest with customer-managed keys only if we can guarantee key usage does not transit Redwood-managed infrastructures. Given current pipeline, I agree we should push for direct-to-customer export for customers needing strict BYOK semantics.

2) Audit trail: whichever path we choose, we need an immutable audit entry (logged to our audit index) showing who toggled sampling, the time window, the justification, and an approval record. This will be critical for our SOC 2 reviewers.

3) UI surface: Product should expose a temporary "Evidence Mode" toggle in Console that sets the sampling override with a required "end date" and an approval email flow. For the pilot, a manual Ops flip is tolerable but we should ship the Console affordance in the medium-term plan.

4) Comms: Ben — can you confirm DataHealth is OK with either: (A) manual ops flip + attestation (fast) or (B) a 3-4 week implementation for direct-to-customer BYOK export (safer)? We should not promise direct BYOK exports in under 3 weeks.

I'll draft the audit requirements and the acceptance criteria for the evidence pack.

-marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: security@datahealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence sampling exemption for pilot

Samir / DataHealth team — quick note from the commercial side.

We can accept the manual Ops flip path for the pilot provided the following are in place before go-live:
- Written attestation that DataHealth understands the staging-bucket caveat and agrees to it for this pilot window
- A clear surcharge line item and an estimate of expected incremental cost (S3 + packaging + engineering oncall)
- A delivery SLA for the evidence pack at pilot exit (we should commit to a 7-business-day window for the pack generation)

If DataHealth requires direct-to-customer BYOK export as a condition of the pilot, we will need to move the pilot start by ~3 weeks to accommodate the engineering work Marissa and Karthik described.

Priya — I'll draft the short commercial addendum and the attestation language and loop in Legal if they want to redline.

-ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
